tool.name: MapBookFeatureIndex
tool.summary: Builds the index (gazetteer) of a map book: for every named feature in one or more layers, the pages it appears on as compact ranges such as "1-3, 12", the grid cells per page, and the number of features with that name in that layer that are on a page (one row per name and layer). Also lists named features that fall on no page and, optionally, a de-duplicated table of chosen field values per page. Read-only.

param.name: index_layer
param.dialogReference: Polygon layer of the map book pages (the map series index layer).

param.name: page_number_field
param.dialogReference: Optional field with the page number. When set, pages are listed by number (whole numbers compress to ranges); otherwise by name (names that are whole numbers compress too).

param.name: feature_layers
param.dialogReference: One or more layers of features to index (points, lines or polygons).

param.name: name_field
param.dialogReference: Name of the field that holds the feature name. It is looked up in every feature layer by exact name first (then the exact name ignoring case), then by alias, then by a loose name match (Unicode NFKC, ignoring case, spaces, dashes, underscores and the Arabic tatweel). When empty, the first text field of the first feature layer called name, street_name, full_name, fullname, feature_name, name_en or name_ar is suggested.

param.name: grid_layer
param.dialogReference: Optional polygon layer of grid cells (for example A1, B1 ...). Cells must be convex polygons (same rule as the pages). A cell may cover several pages. Pages that no cell overlaps with an area, and pages that the cells cover only in part, are named in a warning and counted in the report Summary; a grid with no cell on any page stops the run with an error. When pages overlap and each has its own cells, each page uses its own cells in the overlap (one rule: the cells a page owns do not overlap each other; then the labels, then the ObjectIDs decide).

param.name: grid_label_field
param.dialogReference: Field with the cell label. Required when a grid layer is set.

param.name: per_page_fields
param.dialogReference: Optional field names (looked up in each feature layer like the name field) for the per-page table. Layers without all of them are left out of that table with a warning.

param.name: out_table
param.dialogReference: Output gazetteer table: NAME, LAYER, PAGES, PAGE_COUNT, GRID_REFS (page:cells, pages separated by '; '), FEATURE_COUNT (features with that name in that layer that are on a page), sorted naturally by name, then layer. A page with no page name (and no page number, when a number field is set) is listed in PAGES as 'OID n' (its ObjectID), with a warning that names those ObjectIDs.

param.name: out_unplaced
param.dialogReference: Optional output table of named features that are on no page: LAYER, SRC_OID, NAME.

param.name: out_per_page
param.dialogReference: Optional output table with PAGE plus the per-page fields (as text), one row per distinct combination, features without a name included (a feature whose per-page values are all empty adds no row). Requires Per-Page Fields.

param.name: out_report
param.dialogReference: Optional Excel (.xlsx) report: Summary (counts) and Detail (the gazetteer). Two CSV files are written instead when .csv is chosen or openpyxl is not available.

tool.usage:
Quick start: choose the Index Layer (the pages of the map series) and its Page Name Field, add one or more Feature Layers, check the Name Field (it is suggested from the first layer when that has a field called name) and give an Output Index Table. Everything else is optional: a page number field, a grid layer, a table of named features on no page, a table of values per page and an Excel report.

NOT VERIFIED: use with a Basic licence, the Name Field suggestion in the dialog and the Cancel button.

Notes. Pages come from the index layer of a map series (Grid Index Features or Strip Map Index Features); every page must be a single convex polygon (rectangles, rotated or not). Other pages are refused with their ObjectIDs, grouped by cause (concave, multipart, with holes). A page counts as convex when no vertex lies deeper inside its convex hull than one millionth of the page size (at least 0.5 mm, or 5e-9 degrees in a geographic index), so extra vertices on straight edges and coordinates rounded to the geodatabase resolution are accepted; the page is then used as its convex hull. Anything more concave is refused: in particular a sheet bounded by meridians and parallels and stored with densified edges in a projected system (a projected parallel is a curve), however finely densified, and rotated pages whose extra vertices were moved off the straight edge. Workaround: rebuild the pages as straight-edged 4-corner polygons (Grid Index Features or Strip Map Index Features), or keep graticule sheets in a geographic index. Grid cells follow the same rule, and one refused cell stops the run.

Assignment rule: a line or polygon is on a page only if it runs through the page's interior (a road exactly along the edge between two pages is on neither; a polygon touching a page along an edge is not on it. The run counts such features among the unplaced ones, says so in a message and in the report Summary, so you can see the size of the effect). A point is on every page whose interior or boundary contains it, so a point on a shared edge is listed on both pages. Grid cells use the same rule, within the part of each cell that lies on the page, with one fallback: a feature that is on a page but runs through no cell's interior there (a road exactly on an internal grid line) is listed with the cells that meet it where it runs along the shared edge of two cells, and a message counts such features. A feature in a part of the page that no cell covers gets no cell there, even where it touches a cell at an end or runs along the outer edge of the grid. The fallback applies only when the feature crosses no cell interior on that page: a road that runs along a grid line and then dips a little into one cell is listed with that cell only. Overlapping pages that each have their own grid (strip maps; Strip Map Index Features overlaps pages by 10% by default): one rule decides which page a cell belongs to: the cells a page owns do not overlap each other. A cell can belong only to a page that holds the largest part of it; where cells lie wholly in the overlap, a page is ruled out when the cell overlaps a cell that page already owns, then a cell goes to its one page that has no other cell of that label, then (only when each page's cells are numbered one after the other) the cells between two pages' ObjectIDs are split there so that no page owns two overlapping cells. Page and cell centres are not used. On each page only that page's own cells are used where a neighbouring page's cells reach into them, with a warning. A cell that the rule cannot place (it coincides with a cell of a neighbouring page, its label is unique and the ObjectIDs are not numbered page by page) is used on every page it is on, with a warning that names it; cells that overlap each other on a page are listed with a warning to check the grid. A zero-length line or zero-area polygon is on no page; it is counted separately, not as touching a page edge. A self-intersecting polygon whose parts cancel out (a bow-tie, net area zero) is also on no page and gets a warning to run Repair Geometry. Page and cell labels that contain ',', ';' or ':' (or page labels such as 1-2) make PAGES and GRID_REFS ambiguous and get a warning.

Features are grouped by layer and trimmed name, so a street split into many segments gives one entry; FEATURE_COUNT is the number of features with that name in that layer that are on a page (those on no page are not counted; they are listed in the unplaced output). Canonically equivalent spellings (Unicode NFC, for example u + combining diaeresis and the single letter ü) are the same name, shown as first met. Page lists are in natural order (2 before 10); runs of two or more consecutive whole page numbers become ranges. Features without a name are counted, not indexed, but they do appear in the per-page table. A dataset given twice in Feature Layers (or two layers of one dataset with overlapping definition queries) is read twice, so its features count twice; the run warns when two feature layers read the same dataset. Nothing is measured: all inputs are read in the index layer's own coordinate system (degrees for a geographic index), so page edges stay exactly as stored; in a geographic index 180 and -180 degrees are the same meridian, and in a Web Mercator index x and x +- 40,075,016.69 m (one turn of the equator), so pages drawn across the antimeridian work. Features in another coordinate system are projected vertex by vertex into the index's system, so a long segment becomes a straight chord there (this matters only for long segments close to a page edge; densify such features first). A feature or grid layer with an unknown coordinate system (read with its coordinates as they are) or on another datum than the index (projected without a datum transformation) gets a warning. True curves are densified.

Names and per-page values are cleaned before they are grouped: Unicode NFC, control characters and invisible marks (left-to-right and right-to-left marks, zero width space, byte order mark) removed, runs of spaces and line breaks folded to one space, ends trimmed. "Java Cafe", "Java Cafe" and a copy with a hidden mark are one entry. Page names, page numbers and grid cell labels are cleaned the same way, so a page "5" and a page "5" with a hidden mark are one page label (the warning about page labels used by more than one page names it), and two such cells are one cell in GRID_REFS. The zero width joiner and non-joiner are kept (they change Arabic and Persian letter shapes), but a name made only of such marks and spaces counts as no name; case and Arabic letter variants (alef forms, teh marbuta) are not unified. Entries sort by code point, not by Arabic collation. In the per-page table a field whose name the output already has (ObjectID, and Id or Field1 that ArcGIS Pro adds to a shapefile or dBASE table) is renamed with a number and keeps its original name as the alias; the run says so. Two feature layers with the same layer name are listed under one LAYER value, with a warning. The Cancel button is honoured between steps and after every 500 features: the tool stops, deletes the outputs it created and reports that it was cancelled.

Selections and definition queries on layer inputs are honoured. The inputs are never modified. Existing outputs are replaced only when geoprocessing is allowed to overwrite outputs. An output that is one of the inputs is refused. Tables joined to an input layer are not known by their path (a layer reports only its own table), so any output named like a table of a joined layer is refused, in any workspace; still, never write an output over a joined table.
